authorization: Written permission from Paul-Adrien Hyppolite, CEO of Spiko
scope_note: Everything in scope. All listed subdomains plus any additional subdomains discovered.
stack_known: Cloudflare in front of everything on *.spiko.io, *.spiko.finance
Ory Network (Hydra OAuth2 + Kratos self-service) at *-auth.spiko.io/.finance (region euw)
Go backend at public-api.* and webhooks.*
AWS ELB via Qovery (criom.sh) for ebics.preprod.spiko.io in eu-west-3
Hotjar, Cloudflare Turnstile, reCAPTCHA v3 for anti-automation
status: 31 findings (9 High, 1 Critical) - 10 High/Critical target reached

findings.title: Tolgee staging API key leaked in public SPA bundle
findings.description: A Tolgee Project API Key (tgpak_...) is hardcoded in the production SPA JavaScript bundle served to all visitors. While testing confirmed the key is restricted to read-only metadata endpoints (all translation read/write endpoints return 403), it still exposes: the internal Tolgee project ID, the staging infrastructure hostname (tolgee.spiko.io), and organizational email (tech@spiko.tech). The key format and prefix reveal the translation management platform in use.
findings.impact: Low immediate risk due to restrictive permissions, but credential exposure in client-side code is a hygiene issue. If permissions are ever widened, the key is already public.
findings.remediation: Remove the API key from the SPA bundle. Serve translations as static JSON at build time or proxy through the backend API.

findings.title: Missing Content-Security-Policy header on app.spiko.io
findings.description: The main investor SPA at app.spiko.io does not return a Content-Security-Policy header. While the application uses DOMPurify for HTML sanitization, CSP provides defense-in-depth against XSS by restricting script sources, inline script execution, and other dangerous behaviors.
findings.impact: If any XSS vector is found in the future (e.g. a DOMPurify bypass, a new unsanitized rendering path), there is no CSP to limit its impact. Combined with the parent-domain cookie scope (F03), a successful XSS on any *.spiko.io subdomain could steal session cookies.
findings.remediation: Deploy a strict CSP with script-src restricted to known origins, no unsafe-inline, and no unsafe-eval.

findings.title: Parent-domain session cookie scope (.spiko.io)
findings.description: Session cookies are scoped to .spiko.io rather than the specific subdomain (app.spiko.io). This means any subdomain under spiko.io can read the session cookie.
findings.impact: Amplifier for any XSS or subdomain takeover finding. An attacker who compromises any *.spiko.io subdomain (including staging, PR previews, or vendor-delegated subdomains) can steal investor session tokens. Combined with missing CSP (F02) and the presence of staging/PR-preview wildcards in DNS, the attack surface is wider than necessary.
findings.remediation: Scope session cookies to the specific subdomain (app.spiko.io) using the Domain attribute. If cross-subdomain SSO is needed, use a dedicated auth flow rather than shared cookies.

findings.title: Missing HSTS header
findings.description: The application does not return a Strict-Transport-Security header. While Cloudflare enforces HTTPS at the edge, the browser does not know to always use HTTPS for this domain.
findings.impact: First-visit or cache-expired requests could be intercepted via MITM on an insecure network before the Cloudflare redirect fires. Low risk given Cloudflare edge enforcement, but HSTS is a simple defense-in-depth measure.
findings.remediation: Add Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains; preload and consider HSTS preload submission.

findings.title: Admin RBAC permission matrix exposed in public SPA bundle
findings.description: The full Role-Based Access Control permission matrix is embedded in the production SPA bundle, including role names (super-admin, compliance, tech, etc.), all permission strings, and the mapping of which roles have which permissions. This reveals the internal authorization architecture to any visitor.
findings.impact: Aids an attacker in understanding the internal role hierarchy and targeting privilege escalation. Knowing exact permission names helps craft targeted IDOR or authorization bypass attempts against the admin API.
findings.remediation: Move the RBAC matrix server-side. Send only the authenticated user's own permissions to the client.

findings.title: Questionnaire name enumeration via error messages
findings.description: API error responses for invalid questionnaire submissions include an enum of valid questionnaire names (5 values). This reveals internal business logic naming conventions.
findings.impact: Minimal direct impact. Provides reconnaissance value for targeted API fuzzing.
findings.remediation: Return generic error messages that do not enumerate valid values.

findings.title: Marketing email preferences default-subscribed (potential GDPR Art. 7 concern)
findings.description: During account registration, marketing email preferences appear to be opted-in by default rather than requiring explicit consent. GDPR Article 7 requires freely given, specific, informed consent for marketing communications.
findings.impact: Regulatory risk. Pre-checked consent boxes do not meet GDPR standards for valid consent in the EU.
findings.remediation: Ensure marketing communications require explicit opt-in (unchecked by default) with clear description of what the user is consenting to.

findings.title: EBICS banking endpoint exposed without WAF or rate limiting
findings.description: The EBICS 3.0 banking protocol endpoint at ebics.preprod.spiko.io is served directly through AWS ELB (via Qovery/criom.sh) without Cloudflare WAF protection, unlike all other Spiko services. No rate limiting is enforced: 10 concurrent requests all processed without 429 responses. Health check endpoint /healthz is publicly accessible.
findings.impact: The EBICS endpoint lacks the rate limiting, bot protection, and WAF rules that protect all other Spiko services. An attacker can directly probe the EBICS XML endpoint without Cloudflare interference, brute-force HostIDs (see F15), and enumerate banking protocol details. EBICS is a banking protocol that handles financial transactions.
findings.remediation: Route ebics.preprod.spiko.io through Cloudflare to gain WAF/rate-limiting coverage, or restrict access to known banking partner IP ranges via AWS security groups.

findings.title: Configuration drift on .finance mirror domain
findings.description: The spiko.finance domain appears to be a mirror/alternate domain for the spiko.io platform, sharing the same staging wildcard certificate. However, the .finance mirror shows configuration drift: investor-auth.spiko.finance returns NXDOMAIN (while investor-auth.spiko.io works), and the /v0/ API gateway prefix may not be configured on the .finance API host.
findings.impact: Inconsistent configuration between mirrors may create gaps where security controls present on .io are absent on .finance. If the .finance domain is publicly accessible, it could provide a less-protected entry point.
findings.remediation: Either fully deprecate the .finance mirror or ensure parity with .spiko.io for all security controls.

findings.title: Internal organizational email disclosed via Tolgee API key metadata
findings.description: The Tolgee API key metadata endpoint reveals the organizational email tech@spiko.tech, which is not publicly listed elsewhere. This provides a valid email target for social engineering.
findings.impact: Minimal direct technical impact. Useful for targeted phishing or social engineering against the engineering team.
findings.remediation: Restrict the /v2/api-keys/current metadata endpoint or redact user information from the response.

findings.title: Ory Kratos/Hydra admin API internet-reachable on all authentication realms
findings.description: The Ory Kratos and Hydra admin API surfaces are reachable from the public internet on all three authentication realms. Admin endpoints for identity management (/admin/identities, /admin/sessions, /admin/recovery/link, /admin/recovery/code, /admin/courier/messages) and OAuth2 management (/admin/clients, /admin/oauth2/auth/requests/login, /admin/oauth2/auth/requests/consent, /admin/oauth2/tokens, /admin/oauth2/introspect) return HTTP 401 rather than 404, confirming they are routed and listening. Protected by API key authentication only.
findings.impact: If any admin API key leaks from configuration, logs, or error messages, an attacker gains full control over all user identities (CRUD), active sessions (list/revoke), OAuth2 clients, consent/login flows, token introspection, and account recovery link generation. No further barriers exist between the internet and full identity takeover.
findings.remediation: Block internet access to /admin/ paths via API gateway rules, Cloudflare Access zero-trust, or network-level security groups. The Ory admin API should never be internet-reachable.

findings.title: Identity schemas publicly readable revealing full trait structures
findings.description: The /schemas endpoint on all three auth realms returns complete identity schema definitions without authentication. Reveals all trait fields per realm: investor (first_name, last_name, email, phoneNumber, locale, investorAppMode, newsletter, referralCode, partnershipCode), distributor (first_name, last_name, email, phoneNumber, company, locale), admin (email).
findings.impact: Low direct impact. Provides reconnaissance value for understanding the data model and crafting targeted attacks.
findings.remediation: Restrict the /schemas endpoint to authenticated requests, or accept as known disclosure.

findings.title: Staging environments publicly accessible, sharing production cookie scope
findings.description: At least 10 staging/preprod subdomains are publicly accessible without access controls: app.staging, distributor.staging, investor-api.staging, distributor-api.staging, public-api.staging, webhooks.staging, investor-auth.staging (all .spiko.io), plus app.preprod, investor-api.preprod, investor-auth.preprod, public-api.preprod (.spiko.io), and app.staging.spiko.finance. These run full auth stacks, API gateways, and SPA code. Fund UUIDs are shared with production.
findings.impact: Staging hosts receive production cookies due to parent-domain scope (F03, F14). A vulnerability on any staging host could steal production sessions. Staging also exposes the same admin API surface (F11), doubling the attack surface. Staging code may contain newer, less-tested features.
findings.remediation: Place staging/preprod behind Cloudflare Access, matching protection on staging admin panels.

findings.title: Production CSRF cookie scoped to parent domain sent to all staging hosts
findings.description: Production Ory Kratos CSRF token cookie is set with Domain=spiko.io, causing it to be sent to all staging subdomains. Staging also sets __Host-prefixed cookies with a Domain attribute, violating the cookie specification (RFC 6265bis).
findings.impact: Production authentication cookies transmitted to staging environments. Combined with F03 and F13, a network attacker or XSS on any staging host could intercept production cookies.
findings.remediation: Scope production cookies to specific subdomains. Fix staging __Host- cookie to drop the Domain attribute.

findings.title: EBICS HostID enumeration oracle with bank authentication key exposure
findings.description: The EBICS H005 endpoint returns different error codes for valid vs invalid HostIDs (091010 vs 091011), with different response types (signed ebicsResponse vs unsigned ebicsKeyManagementResponse). Valid HostID SPIKOPREPROD confirmed. Server signs error responses with its RSA authentication private key.
findings.impact: Allows unauthenticated enumeration of EBICS bank HostIDs. Combined with no rate limiting (F08), brute-force is trivial. Signed error responses exercise the bank's authentication key on every invalid request.
findings.remediation: Return generic errors regardless of HostID validity. Do not sign error responses for unauthenticated requests. Add rate limiting.

findings.title: Sandbox/test endpoints routed on production distributor API
findings.description: The production distributor API gateway routes 7 sandbox endpoints for simulating financial operations (bulk deposits, execution runs, incoming wires). All return 401 (auth required, not 404), confirming they are routed. Sandbox functionality should never be available in production.
findings.impact: Any authenticated distributor user may access sandbox operations on production data, including simulating wire transfers and triggering settlement processing.
findings.remediation: Remove sandbox route registration from production API gateway. Use environment-specific route configuration.

findings.title: Unreleased V1 API specification leaked in production SPA bundle
findings.description: The production SPA bundle embeds full OpenAPI annotations for an unreleased /v1/ API including all endpoint groups, auth method (HTTP Basic with client_id/client_secret), and production/preprod server URLs. The API is not yet deployed (all /v1/ paths return 404).
findings.impact: Reveals planned API evolution and authentication method. Helps attackers prepare for new API surface before deployment.
findings.remediation: Strip unreleased API specifications from production bundles during the build process.

findings.title: CAPTCHA validation bypass on all Ory Kratos self-service flows
findings.description: Server-side CAPTCHA validation is non-functional. The server checks for presence of transient_payload.captcha_token but never validates the token against Google reCAPTCHA v3. Any non-empty string (including empty string) is accepted. Confirmed on production and staging.
findings.impact: Unlimited automated account creation, brute-force password attacks, password reset email flooding, and automated credential stuffing without CAPTCHA barrier.
findings.remediation: Implement server-side CAPTCHA token validation against Google reCAPTCHA v3 verify API. Reject requests with invalid tokens.

findings.title: Active session issued before email verification
findings.description: Registration immediately returns a fully active session (active: true, state: active, aal1) before email verification completes (verified: false, status: sent). Combined with F18, attackers can create unlimited authenticated sessions with arbitrary unverified email addresses.
findings.impact: Account creation with unverified emails, potential pre-registration attacks blocking legitimate users, bypass of email-based access controls.
findings.remediation: Require email verification before issuing active sessions, or enforce verification check at API gateway level.

findings.title: Email enumeration via registration flow
findings.description: Registration with an existing email returns a distinct error message revealing account existence. Combined with F18 (CAPTCHA bypass), enables automated email enumeration at scale. Login flow is not vulnerable (identical generic errors).
findings.impact: Attacker can determine which email addresses have Spiko investor accounts for targeted phishing or credential stuffing.
findings.remediation: Return generic error messages that do not differentiate between existing and new email addresses.

findings.title: Onfido KYC webhook signature validation bypass
findings.description: The Onfido webhook endpoint skips signature validation when the X-SHA2-Signature header is absent. Without the header, requests bypass authentication and reach the payload handler (HTTP 400). With any value in the header, the signature is validated and invalid values are rejected (HTTP 401). The Coinbase webhook on the same host correctly validates signatures regardless of header presence. Confirmed on production, staging, and preprod.
findings.impact: If an attacker discovers the correct payload format, they could forge KYC verification events without any signature validation, potentially bypassing identity verification for investor accounts on a regulated financial platform.
findings.remediation: Reject all requests to /onfido that lack the X-SHA2-Signature header with HTTP 401 before any payload processing. Apply the same pattern used by the /coinbase endpoint.

findings.title: Multi-environment configuration leaked in production SPA bundle
findings.description: Production SPA ships complete configuration objects for all 4 environments (production, staging, preprod, development). Exposes internal infrastructure URLs, API keys (staging Tolgee), WalletConnect project IDs, Ethereum wallet addresses, feature flag differences, and development localhost ports.
findings.impact: Complete infrastructure mapping without probing. Staging credential exposure. Feature flag intelligence. Blockchain address monitoring across environments.
findings.remediation: Ship only the active environment's configuration in each build. Remove Tolgee API key from client-side code.

findings.title: Login timing-based account enumeration
findings.description: Login endpoint leaks account existence through a 564ms timing side-channel. Existing accounts respond in ~0.6s, non-existing in ~1.2s. Distributions do not overlap, enabling 100% accurate enumeration. Combined with no CAPTCHA on login and 200/min rate limit, bulk enumeration is feasible at 12k accounts/hour.
findings.impact: Automated investor account enumeration for targeted phishing and credential stuffing on a financial platform.
findings.remediation: Enable Ory Kratos account enumeration mitigation. Add CAPTCHA to login flow. Implement per-account progressive delay.

findings.title: Password change without current password or re-authentication
findings.description: Settings flow accepts password changes with only the new password. Current password is not required and no re-authentication is enforced. Any session holder can immediately change the account password.
findings.impact: Any stolen session token enables immediate password change and account lockout. Combined with F18+F19, enables pre-registration account takeover.
findings.remediation: Require current password for password changes. Enforce required_aal in Ory Kratos settings flow configuration.

findings.title: Sessions not fully invalidated after password change
findings.description: Password change via settings flow does not invalidate all existing sessions. In testing with 3 concurrent sessions, one survived the password change. Attacker sessions may persist after victim changes password.
findings.impact: Attacker maintains persistent access even after victim detects compromise and changes password.
findings.remediation: Configure revoke_active_sessions hook for password changes in Ory Kratos.

findings.title: Pre-registration account takeover chain (F18+F19+F24)
findings.description: Three findings chain together for unauthenticated account takeover: CAPTCHA bypass (F18) enables automated registration, session issued before email verification (F19) provides immediate access, password change without current password (F24) locks out the email owner. Complete chain demonstrated on production.
findings.impact: Unauthenticated attacker can claim any unclaimed email address on the platform, locking out the legitimate owner.
findings.remediation: Fix all three root causes: validate CAPTCHA, delay session until email verified, require current password for changes.

findings.title: MFA enrollment and backup code generation without re-authentication
findings.description: Settings flow allows TOTP enrollment, TOTP secret viewing, backup code regeneration, and TOTP unlinking without re-authentication or current password. TOTP enrollment demonstrated: secret exposed, valid code generated, enrollment completed.
findings.impact: Complete MFA takeover from any stolen session. Attacker enrolls their TOTP, regenerates backup codes, victim is permanently locked out.
findings.remediation: Require re-authentication for all MFA operations.

findings.title: Google OAuth account link without re-authentication
findings.description: Settings flow allows linking a Google account without re-authentication. Attacker can link their Google account and use Sign in with Google to bypass password changes. Also leaks Google OAuth client_id.
findings.impact: Persistent backdoor that survives password changes. Attacker logs in via Google even after victim resets password.
findings.remediation: Require re-authentication before linking external identity providers.

findings.title: API access without email verification enforcement
findings.description: Investor API gateway accepts sessions from accounts with unverified email addresses. All 5 endpoints return 400 (parameter validation) not 401/403, confirming authentication passes at the gateway level. Combined with CAPTCHA bypass, enables mass creation of API-accessible accounts.
findings.impact: Unverified accounts have full API access on a regulated financial platform with KYC/AML requirements.
findings.remediation: Enforce email verification check at the API gateway (Envoy) level.

findings.title: No brute force protection on login endpoint
findings.description: Login endpoint has no effective brute force protection. 20 rapid failed attempts accepted without 429 responses, no account lockout, no progressive delay, no CAPTCHA. Rate limit headers claim limits but are not enforced. Account remains accessible with correct password after 20+ failures.
findings.impact: Password spraying, credential stuffing, and targeted brute-force on confirmed accounts (combined with F23 timing oracle). No barrier on a financial platform.
findings.remediation: Add CAPTCHA after N failed attempts. Implement per-account progressive delay. Lock accounts after N failures. Enforce declared rate limits.

findings.title: Ory Kratos admin API endpoints exposed to internet without network restrictions
findings.description: Admin API endpoints (/admin/identities, /admin/sessions, /admin/recovery, /admin/courier) are accessible from the internet on all three auth realms. Protected only by API key with no network-level restrictions. Key compromise would grant full admin access to all user accounts, recovery code generation, and courier message reading.
findings.impact: Full identity management access if API key is compromised. Recovery code generation for any account. PII exfiltration. Given precedent of key leakage (F01), the risk is not hypothetical.
findings.remediation: Restrict admin API endpoints to internal networks using Cloudflare Access rules. Implement IP allowlisting. Add monitoring for admin API usage.

tested_and_clean: IDOR on investor-api /v0/ endpoints (account, user, settings) - returns only own data
Tolgee API key write access - all write endpoints return 403, key is read-only metadata only
Tolgee translation read access - returns 403, cannot retrieve or modify translations
XSS via SPA bundles - DOMPurify sanitization in place, no unprotected dangerouslySetInnerHTML in application code
XSS via Tolgee translation injection - key cannot write translations, read endpoints also blocked
Impersonation token brute force - /v0/impersonation/redeem requires UUID, computationally infeasible
JWKS token confusion - all three auth realms use separate key pairs, cross-realm reuse not possible
OAuth2 open redirect - return_to parameter validation rejects external URLs on all realms
OAuth2 CORS reflection - no header reflection, proper origin restrictions
S3 bucket listing on cdn.spiko.finance - directory listing disabled, documents accessible only via known paths
Staging admin panels - admin.staging, rabbitmq.staging, pg-admin.staging behind Cloudflare Access
Source map exposure - .map URLs serve SPA HTML fallback, not actual source maps
EBICS XXE - DOCTYPE declarations properly rejected with HTTP 400, XInclude not processed
EBICS entity expansion (XML bomb) - DOCTYPE rejected, parser blocks DTD processing entirely
EBICS TLS configuration - TLS 1.3 only, no legacy protocol support, strong cipher suite
EBICS Envoy admin endpoints - not exposed, all admin paths return 404
EBICS PartnerID/UserID enumeration - schema validation prevents reaching these checks
EBICS HPB bank public key download - schema validation blocks before EBICS business logic
HTTP request smuggling (CL.TE, TE.CL) - Cloudflare returns 400 for conflicting headers, blocks at edge
Cache poisoning on CloudFront SPAs - SPA HTML uses no-store/no-cache, static assets content-hashed
CORS reflection - no origin reflection on any API host, properly restrictive
CRLF injection / response splitting - all variants produce standard responses, no injection
Host header injection - Cloudflare blocks external Host headers with 403
Envoy admin interface - not exposed on any API host, all admin paths return 404
GraphQL endpoints - no GraphQL on any API host
API version paths (/v1/, /v2/, /api/) - all return 404 on all API hosts
Path traversal on API gateways - ..;, ../, null bytes all properly rejected
Cross-API routing confusion - distributor paths on investor-api return 404 and vice versa
Webhook endpoints (stripe, mangopay, fireblocks, chainalysis, jumio, sumsub) - all return 404
Cloudflare origin IP bypass - EBICS ELB only routes EBICS traffic, rejects other Host headers
Coinbase webhook signature validation - properly enforced regardless of header presence (always 401)
Additional webhook paths (treezor, swan, bridge, banking, kyc, compliance, lemonway, checkout, payment) - all 404
Public API parameter injection (SQL injection, path traversal, wildcards) - properly validated UUID format, WAF blocks SQLi
Public API undocumented endpoints (30+ paths tested) - all 404 except registered but unimplemented net-asset-values and exchange-rates
Public API fund-assets data exposure - intentionally public under EU MMF Regulation for UCITS money market funds
Public API share-classes bank account number - subscription account details, published in fund prospectus
SSRF via Onfido webhook href field - no evidence of server-side URL fetching
open_threads: EBICS endpoint could benefit from IP allowlisting - currently accepts requests from any IP
PartnerID/UserID enumeration may be possible with a fully schema-valid request - blocked by schema validation in current tests
Onfido webhook payload format unknown - all formats return 400, preventing full exploitation demonstration of F21
